text:
Carolina arrives in Calgary controlling the chances while Calgary is giving them up. At five on five, CAR has taken 57% of the expected goals to CGY's 50%, and the Flames allow 3.36 expected goals per 60 against Carolina's 2.51. The model projects 3.49 goals for CAR tonight and 2.67 for CGY. The Hurricanes are on the second night of a back-to-back after a 3-2 win in Winnipeg, and they are missing Taylor Hall and Jordan Staal, though the model has priced all of that in. Calgary has taken 5.1 penalties a game, a problem against a power play that generates 1.02 expected goals a game, while the Flames' own power play makes just 0.26.

In net, projected starter Dustin Wolf (CGY) is at -8.0 goals saved above expected this season and -2.8 last year, and the Flames are 1-4-0 in their last five with 50% of the expected goals. Projected CAR starter Brandon Bussi is at -1.9 this season after +1.2 in 39 games last year, so neither goalie arrives on solid footing, but Wolf's slide is far steeper.

Carolina is 5-0-0 in its last five with more expected goals in every game, averaging a 61% share. The storyline that Carolina has won seven straight is not something the model prices, so treat it as color rather than a deciding factor. Andrei Svechnikov leads the Hurricanes at 40% to score and 66% to record a point, helped by his top power-play role. Calgary's best looks come from Joel Farabee, Morgan Frost and Matt Coronato, each around 22% to 23% to score.
